contracts.title: GET/HEAD discovery
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented (2026-10-13): no HEAD. One GET with `Range: bytes=OFFSET-` both verifies range support and supplies data; the validated 206 body is adopted by the segment starting at OFFSET (a resume probes from the first missing byte). A 200 body is streamed directly. Only a malformed 206 or 416 triggers one further full GET. [Engine fixture](../tests/integration/http_engine.py) counts requests: one request for a one-connection file and for no-range servers.

contracts.title: HTTP methods and request bodies
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: `Options.method/body` and CLI `--method/--data-file` replay the method and a bounded (1 MiB) body on every probe/range request; GET with body, HEAD/CONNECT/TRACE/OPTIONS are rejected; 301/302/303 on a non-GET request fails instead of becoming GET, 307/308 preserve it. Context hash covers method/body. Fixture verifies POST-only file with 4 connections, 307 and refused 302. Daemon/browser submissions do not yet carry method/body.

contracts.title: One-shot and expiring URLs
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: request adoption means a ranged or full one-shot link is fetched by the probe response alone. If extra range connections are refused (401/403/404/410 on their first request), those ranges are released and the adopted open-ended stream absorbs adjacent untouched ranges; fixture `oneshot.bin` (8 connections) and `oneshot-norange.bin` succeed with one accepted request. No request-token lease, expiry detection or site rules.

contracts.title: Range capability and boundaries
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented static path: strict Content-Range parser, bounded segments, identity encoding, exact body coverage. Accept-Ranges alone is not used as proof.

contracts.title: Ignored or malformed partial response
contracts.current_behavior: Different: malformed probe can fall back to full transfer; malformed worker response fails and retains checkpoint. No automatic verified single-stream restart after worker corruption.

contracts.title: Representation compression
contracts.current_behavior: Restricted: sends Accept-Encoding identity and rejects nonidentity final/range responses. Cargo has no reqwest compression feature.

contracts.title: Known and unknown response length
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: unknown size streams the adopted full response until EOF with total/ETA unknown; zero-length resources (416 to the open range) complete as empty files; no resumable metadata for non-range content.

contracts.title: Redirect chains and credentials
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: maximum ten hops; Referer is not rewritten on redirect. Cookie/Authorization/UA/Referer/Accept(-Language) may follow cross-origin redirects because the client strips Cookie/Authorization on host change (fixture verifies the redirected host receives no Cookie); any other custom header stops cross-origin redirects, and any supplied header stops an HTTPS→HTTP downgrade.

contracts.title: Completion success/failure/manual-stop rules
contracts.current_behavior: Partial (2026-10-13): per-queue cycle state (`idle/running/completed/completed_with_failures/stopped`) with one event per execution (`queue events ID`). Success runs the configured completion action through an injectable adapter: the real OS adapter by default, a recording adapter under `XDM_FAKE_OS_ACTIONS=1` so tests never touch the OS. Settable actions: none, notify, sleep, hibernate, shutdown, restart, exit and program (path plus literal argument list). Failures, manual stop (including global stop) and schedule cutoff record the event with action `suppressed`; an empty start produces no event; new work after completion starts a new cycle; an edited or canceled countdown records `cancelled`. Destructive actions additionally require the per-queue `--confirm-destructive` opt-in and their countdown (Q17). The [completion fixture](../tests/integration/completion_actions.py) with the recording adapter covers notify recorded, unconfirmed shutdown rejected, countdown visible then recorded, cancel prevents and manual stop suppresses; daemon unit tests cover empty-start, new-cycle, final-failure and daemon-restart suppression.

contracts.title: Completion program/file launch
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented (2026-10-13): `queue completion ID program PATH [ARGS...]` stores the executable plus a literal argument list (IPC `CompletionAction::Program`, at most 64 arguments) and launches it without a shell after a qualifying completion, spawned without blocking the daemon while a reaper thread collects the exit status; the queue event records `started`, `executed` or the spawn error. The path is configured per queue, never browser-supplied. The completion fixture launches a real script through the recording adapter and asserts every argument arrives literally, spaces and shell metacharacters (`a;b

contracts.title: Disconnect modem/VPN and app exit
contracts.current_behavior: Partial: the modem/VPN disconnect action remains missing (no dial-up or VPN adapter and no connection scoping). The application-exit action exists: `queue completion ID exit` ends the daemon about 300 ms after the queue completion event so the event insert and reply frame are written first; it needs no destructive opt-in, its configuration is unit-tested, and the recording adapter logs it instead of exiting, so no fixture terminates the daemon.

contracts.title: Shutdown/restart/sleep/hibernate
contracts.current_behavior: Implemented (2026-10-13): sleep, hibernate, shutdown and restart are settable per queue but require explicit opt-in (`--confirm-destructive`, otherwise the command is rejected) plus a persistent cancelable countdown (default 60 s; the daemon accepts 1..86400 s). During the countdown the event reads `pending`, `CompletionStatus` reports queue, action and `seconds_remaining`, and `CompletionCancel` cancels it (`cancelled`); a manual stop, final failure, new cycle, action edit or daemon restart suppresses it without executing. The real adapter spawns commands directly with no shell: Linux uses `notify-send` for notify and `systemctl suspend`/`hibernate`/`poweroff`/`reboot`; the Windows path (PowerShell toast with `msg` fallback, `rundll32 powrprof.dll,SetSuspendState`, `shutdown` `/h` `/s` `/r`) is compile-structural only and untested on Windows. Tests run with `XDM_FAKE_OS_ACTIONS=1` recording adapter: the [completion fixture](../tests/integration/completion_actions.py) verifies notify recorded, unconfirmed shutdown rejected, countdown visible then recorded, cancel prevents and manual stop suppresses, and a daemon unit test proves the real adapter never executes an unarmed power action. File, queue and project completion actions remain absent.
